editorial:
Detective Zeke Banks is a cop who doesn't play by the rules, and when a killer starts copying the city's old Saw-style murders, he gets pulled into a deadly game. Working with a fresh-faced rookie partner, Zeke has to figure out who is behind the traps before more people die. The movie brings back the creepy puzzle-box feel of the old Saw films but wraps it in a gritty police story. You'll see plenty of blood, twisted traps, and a mystery that keeps you guessing.

Chris Rock leads the cast with a surprisingly serious turn, and Samuel L. Jackson shows up as Zeke's legendary father. The pacing moves fast, though some of the dialogue feels a bit clunky. The traps are creative but not as wild as the original films. If you enjoy dark crime thrillers with a horror edge, this one is worth your time.
endingExplained: In the final act, you learn that Zeke's rookie partner, William Schenk, is actually the killer. He was a kid whose father was killed by a corrupt cop, and he wants to clean up the police force by punishing bad officers. Schenk traps Zeke and forces him to choose between saving his father or stopping the cycle. Zeke refuses to kill Schenk, but Schenk escapes. The movie ends with Schenk broadcasting his message, leaving Zeke broken and the city on edge.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves dark crime thrillers with a horror edge.
